I think of myself as someone who is a team with my emotions, who works with them. Of course, being human, they overwhelm me on occasion. Of course, having responsibilities, I must sometimes subjugate them to my will. But mostly they are a helpful tool. There are certainly people who manage them better than I do, but I'm at a pretty good place with them.

How did I get to this point? 2 major things:

1) I had a hard youth and had to face a lot of challenges. Initially, this made my relationship with my emotions pretty chaotic. But as I got older and had to overcome these challenges, it put a lot of things into perspective. The little, petty challenges of everyday life started to feel small in comparison to the things I'd already fought through, so my emotional reaction to them became much more manageable.

2) Meditation. I started having clearer thoughts, more focus, and a wider awareness of what I was feeling and why. I began to be able to calm myself and assess where my emotions were useful, and where they were trying to be useful but I didn't understand them. In time, with practice, I was able to start satisfying the problems that my harder emotions were trying to tell me about in more effective ways. Once this became a habit, my feelings naturally drew me to these patterns of thoughts and behaviors that were more healthy and useful.

So, my advice - face challenges, work to be self-aware, appreciate that your emotions are there for a reason, and learn to use them as tools. Be patient and persistent with it.
